findings.finding: Inclusive dance classes challenge traditional ableist notions of dance as spectacle.
findings.quote: This paper focuses on the aim of developing inclusive approaches to dance classes that challenge "ableist" notions of dance as spectacle

findings.finding: Participants experiencing disability value learning climates that promote autonomy and belonging.
findings.quote: Participant value was considered to be enhanced via a learning climate affording opportunities for developing autonomy and a sense of belonging.

findings.finding: Lack of interest is a primary reason reported by students for being inactive during recess.
findings.quote: Among 977 students with inactive recess, the most frequent reasons were lack of interest (40.3%) and absence of games, equipment, or a suitable place (29.1%).

principle: Inclusive dance programs can be developed to challenge ableist notions and support motor and social functioning by fostering environments with no wrong way to move.
for_the_teacher: Design lessons to ensure there is no wrong way to move, removing ableist expectations of how movement should look.
Foster a climate that supports learner autonomy and a strong sense of belonging.
